title: See how the first key part steers new writes
description: Choose a workload and a key shape. The model places the same 64 illustrative inserts into eight logical key ranges so you can compare write concentration with query locality.

workloads.label: New order service
workloads.detail: Generate globally unique IDs; order recency is queried through an index.
workloads.question: How should a new service generate order identities without creating an insert edge?

workloads.label: Legacy integer migration
workloads.detail: Keep INT64 identifiers, but their numeric order has no business meaning.
workloads.question: How can the migration retain integer keys while distributing new values?

workloads.label: High-volume tenant timeline
workloads.detail: Preserve tenant and time-range access while one tenant may produce heavy writes.
workloads.question: How can writes spread without losing the ability to rebuild a tenant timeline?

strategies.label: Monotonic ID first
strategies.detail: An auto-incrementing number or timestamp leads the primary key.
strategies.queryConsequence: Recent rows are adjacent, but every new insert targets the moving end of one key range.

new-orders.title: The key creates a moving write hotspot
new-orders.detail: Adding compute does not change the fact that all new keys first arrive at one edge of the sorted key space.

legacy-integers.title: Preserving numeric order preserves the hotspot
legacy-integers.detail: Use a bit-reversed sequence when integer order is not a business contract.

tenant-timeline.title: Time first concentrates every tenant
tenant-timeline.detail: A globally increasing timestamp leads all inserts to the same range, even when tenant IDs differ later in the key.

strategies.label: Generated UUID version 4
strategies.detail: Use a random UUID as the leading primary-key value.
strategies.queryConsequence: Writes spread, but tenant or time scans need a secondary index because related rows are not adjacent by primary key.

new-orders.title: A direct fit for new independent identities
new-orders.detail: Spanner recommends UUID version 4 for new primary keys when unordered unique identity matches the application.

legacy-integers.title: Good distribution, wider migration
legacy-integers.detail: The write shape is healthy, but changing INT64 identities to UUID affects schemas, APIs, foreign keys, and downstream consumers.

tenant-timeline.title: Writes spread, timeline locality moves to an index
tenant-timeline.detail: A secondary index can restore tenant-time access, but the index design and a very hot tenant still need measurement.

strategies.label: Bit-reversed positive sequence
strategies.detail: Generate unique INT64 values from a sequence, then distribute their high-order bits.
strategies.example: (OrderId INT64 GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY (BIT_REVERSED_POSITIVE))
strategies.queryConsequence: The key remains an integer but no longer preserves creation order; query recency through a timestamp index.

new-orders.title: Useful only when integer identity is a real constraint
new-orders.detail: UUID version 4 is the simpler default for a new service; choose the sequence when INT64 compatibility matters.

legacy-integers.title: Retain INT64 without a monotonic insert edge
legacy-integers.detail: A bit-reversed positive sequence preserves unique integer values while distributing newly generated keys.

tenant-timeline.title: Healthy identity distribution, no tenant locality
tenant-timeline.detail: The timeline still needs an alternate tenant-time access path, and its index can become the next hotspot.

strategies.label: Hash-sharded composite key
strategies.detail: Lead with a stable bucket, then tenant and descending event time.
strategies.queryConsequence: Writes spread across buckets; a complete tenant timeline must query each bucket and merge the ordered results.

new-orders.title: Distribution with unnecessary read fan-out
new-orders.detail: A generated UUID provides distribution without making every identity lookup or timeline query understand buckets.

legacy-integers.title: Possible, but application-visible
legacy-integers.detail: A new bucket prefix changes every key reference and query shape; a bit-reversed sequence is narrower when order is irrelevant.

tenant-timeline.title: Trade write spread for bounded read fan-out
tenant-timeline.detail: Use a small measured bucket count, query all buckets for a full timeline, and merge results by event time.
